title: Most People Miss This About Judah Suggesting the Sale
paragraphs: Most People Miss This About Judah Suggesting the Sale

He didn’t throw the stone.
He made a deal.
That’s what most people miss about Judah suggesting they sell Joseph in Book of Genesis 37.

It looks like mercy.
But it was still betrayal.

“Why kill him?” Judah says.
“Let’s profit from him.”
Pause.

That’s not compassion.
That’s calculated sin dressed as wisdom.

He spared Joseph’s life—
but still crushed his destiny… or so it seemed.
And here’s the uncomfortable truth:

Some of us don’t destroy people outright.
We just compromise them.

We don’t pull the trigger—
we just sign the deal.

We don’t “hate”—
we just justify.
But here’s what we miss…

God was not absent in that pit.
He was writing a bigger story.

Joseph’s chains became the pathway to purpose.
The betrayal became the bridge to salvation for many.
And Judah?

The same Judah who sold his brother…
would later offer himself as a substitute for Benjamin (Genesis 44).

That’s not coincidence.
That’s redemption.

And generations later—
from Judah’s bloodline—came Jesus Christ.
The Lion of Judah.
Let that sink in.

The man who sold his brother…
became part of the lineage of the Savior who would be sold for us.
That’s the Gospel.

We are all Judah.
We’ve all traded truth for convenience.
Chose profit over purity.
Silence over righteousness.
But Jesus—

He steps into our story.
Takes the price of our betrayal.
And offers mercy we never earned.

Not a deal.
A cross.

So if you’ve compromised…
if you’ve justified…
if you’ve been the one who “didn’t kill—but still hurt”—
Grace is still calling your name.

Repent.
Return.
Be rewritten.

Because God doesn’t cancel Judahs.
He redeems them.
